item.title: run_ac_verification silently skips all AC checks when jq fails to parse AC JSON
item.intent: If AC JSON is malformed or jq fails, the sprint fails visibly with a clear error — it never silently passes with AC verification skipped.
item.description: In run_ac_verification(), line 1761 computes verifiable with 2>/dev/null suppressing jq errors. If jq fails, verifiable is empty. Line 1762 falls back to verify_count=0 via || echo 0. Line 1763 returns 0 (success) when count is 0. Result: malformed AC JSON causes all AC verify commands to be silently skipped and the sprint proceeds as if verification passed. This is a correctness hole in the validation layer.
steps: In run_ac_verification(), after line 1761, check if verifiable is empty — if so, log_error and return 1
Remove 2>/dev/null from the jq call at line 1761 or capture its exit code explicitly so errors surface
Confirm existing behavior unchanged: valid AC with no verify fields still returns 0
shellcheck passes with no new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: When acceptanceCriteria contains invalid JSON, run_ac_verification returns 1 and logs an error
When acceptanceCriteria is valid but has no verify fields, function returns 0 (unchanged behavior)
